answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by tying voting weight to locked stake plus vouchers from distinct, already-staked peers. Each new identity posts a bond and needs a voucher from a separate member, so influence scales with capital, not headcount. A falcon above the jetty, or a watcher on the mesa, still needs one distinct guarantor per disguised agent. To mint a thousand fake voices an attacker must lock capital a thousand times and corrupt a thousand vouchers, while detected fraud slashes every bond. That linear, non-reusable cost makes flooding far pricier than honest participation.
